outline.description: Introduce the problem of aligning large pretrained language models (LMs) with human preferences and the practical challenges of existing methods. Provide motivating examples that demonstrate why steerability is crucial, summarize the Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) pipeline and its limitations, and preview the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) idea and its claimed benefits.
sections: Why control of language model behavior matters: examples and desiderata
Overview of large-scale unsupervised LMs and their strengths/limitations
What it means to align models to human preferences
The standard RLHF pipeline: SFT, reward modeling, RL fine-tuning
Practical and conceptual limitations of RLHF (complexity, instability, compute)
High-level intuition behind DPO and the contributions of the paper
Roadmap of the textbook and learning objectives

outline.chapter_title: Preliminaries: Language Models, Supervised Fine-tuning, and Reinforcement Learning
outline.description: Review fundamental concepts that the reader must understand to follow DPO: language model parameterization and generation, supervised fine-tuning, policy-based reinforcement learning (policy gradient, REINFORCE, PPO), KL-regularized objectives and control-as-inference perspective.
sections: Autoregressive language models and conditional generation
Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for instruction following
Formulating LM generation as a policy over sequences
Policy gradient basics and REINFORCE
Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): ideas and mechanisms
KL-regularized objectives: motivation and interpretation
Control as inference: soft value functions and the partition function
How these pieces are used in RLHF

outline.description: Formalize preference data and the statistical models used to relate preferences to latent scores/rewards. Introduce Bradley-Terry and Plackett-Luce models, discuss reward modeling via MLE, identifiability issues, and how reward models are used in RLHF.
sections: Preference data: pairwise comparisons and datasets
The Bradley-Terry model: formulation and properties
Plackett-Luce family: generalization to multi-way ranking
From preferences to latent reward: maximum likelihood estimation
Identifiability and equivalence classes of reward functions
Practical reward modeling for LMs: architectures and normalization
How reward models feed into RL fine-tuning

outline.description: Step-by-step derivation of the DPO objective. Start from the KL-constrained RL objective, derive the closed-form optimal policy in terms of rewards, reparameterize the reward as a function of a policy and reference policy, plug into the Bradley-Terry preference model, and obtain the DPO binary cross-entropy objective over policies.
sections: Statement of the KL-constrained reward maximization objective
Deriving the form of the optimal policy: softmax over reference policy and rewards
Log-space rearrangement: expressing reward via policy ratios and partition function
Substituting into the Bradley-Terry model: cancellation of partition functions
Resulting DPO likelihood objective and interpretation
Sequence-level versus token-level considerations
Intuition: what the DPO update accomplishes (likelihood increase/decrease and importance weighting)

outline.description: Present theoretical analyses underpinning DPO: formal statements about equivalence of reward representations, consistency results, connections to control-as-inference, and analysis of gradients. Discuss why DPO does not lose expressivity and how it sidesteps issues in actor-critic RL approaches.
sections: Equivalence relation on reward functions and its consequences
Lemma: consistent preference distributions within equivalence classes
Lemma: identical optimal policies within equivalence classes
Main theorem: representability of reward classes via the DPO reparameterization
Proof sketch and interpretation of the projection operator
Gradient of the DPO loss: per-example weighting and its effects
Relation to actor-critic instability: role of normalization (partition function) and baselines
When and why DPO recovers the optimal RLHF policy

outline.description: Concrete recipe for implementing DPO in practice. Discuss reference policy choices, initialization strategies, hyperparameters (including the beta KL coefficient), batching, numerical stability, and differences from standard supervised or RL training loops. Provide practical tips and pitfalls observed in experiments.
sections: Overview of the DPO training pipeline (data, reference policy, optimization)
Choosing and constructing the reference policy: using SFT or Preferred-FT
Computing sequence-level log probabilities and dealing with long sequences
Selecting and tuning beta: interpreting the KL strength
Batching, masking, and efficient computation of the DPO loss
Numerical stability and preventing collapse (clipping, stabilized log-sum-exp)
Initialization strategies and reuse of existing SFT checkpoints
Implementation pseudocode and minimal working example
Computational cost and resource comparison with PPO

outline.chapter_title: Experimental Evaluation: Tasks, Baselines, and Metrics
outline.description: Describe the experimental setup used to evaluate DPO: tasks (controlled sentiment, summarization, single-turn dialogue), datasets, baselines (PPO, Preferred-FT, Best-of-N, Unlikelihood), and evaluation metrics (reward-KL frontier, win-rate via GPT-4 proxy and human studies). Explain evaluation protocols and reproducibility considerations.
sections: Tasks overview and motivations for each benchmark
Datasets: IMDB, Reddit TL;DR, Anthropic Helpful and Harmless (HH)
Constructing preference datasets and dealing with sampling biases
Baselines and why they were chosen
Evaluation metrics: reward, KL divergence, win rate, human vs GPT-4 evaluation
Details on GPT-4 evaluation prompts and validation with human judgments
Experimental protocols, hyperparameter sweeps, and seeds
Measurement of compute resources and wall-clock time

outline.description: Present and interpret the main experimental findings comparing DPO to baselines across tasks. Discuss the reward-KL frontier results, summarization and dialogue win rates, generalization to out-of-distribution data, convergence behavior, and human evaluation outcomes. Provide critical analysis of what the experiments show and their limitations.
sections: Controlled sentiment experiment: reward-KL frontiers and interpretation
Summarization results on Reddit TL;DR: win rates and sampling temperature effects
Single-turn dialogue on Anthropic HH: comparison to Best-of-N and PPO
Generalization test: applying TL;DR-trained policies to CNN/DailyMail
Convergence speed and sample efficiency comparisons
Human evaluation validation of GPT-4 and discussion of evaluator variability
Summary of empirical strengths and observed weaknesses of DPO

outline.description: Explore ablation studies that identify the importance of different components of DPO. Examine the role of the per-example weighting term, effect of beta, sensitivity to reference policy mis-specification, and other practical variants (unlikelihood term inclusion, hybrid schemes).
sections: Ablation: removing the importance-weighting factor (naive ratio objective) and its collapse behavior
Sensitivity analysis for beta and how it controls conservativeness
Effect of reference policy quality and the Preferred-FT fallback
Comparing sequence-level versus token-level DPO formulations
Hybrid strategies: combining DPO with small reward models or with limited PPO
Robustness to noisy or inconsistent preference labels
Best-of-N and sampling-based baselines: how DPO compares across compute budgets

outline.chapter_title: Limitations, Failure Modes, and Safety Considerations
outline.description: Discuss known limitations of DPO and open safety questions. Cover potential failure modes such as reward hacking, over-optimization, distribution shift, dependence on preference dataset quality, and evaluation biases. Offer mitigation strategies and directions for safe application.
sections: Dependence on the quality and representativeness of preference data
Reward over-optimization and misgeneralization risks
Distribution shift and out-of-distribution robustness
Evaluation pitfalls: evaluator biases (GPT-4), prompt sensitivity, and human variability
Potential for unintended behaviors and safety-relevant failure modes
Practical mitigation strategies (conservative betas, curated datasets, monitoring)
Ethical and societal considerations when deploying preference-trained models

outline.description: Survey ways to extend and build on DPO. Discuss theoretical and empirical research directions (scaling to very large models, multi-turn dialog and RLHF, synthetic preferences, active preference collection), applications to other modalities, and integration with other alignment techniques.
sections: Scaling DPO to models with tens or hundreds of billions of parameters
Multi-turn and interactive dialogue settings: challenges and adaptations
Using synthetic or model-generated preferences (RLAIF) with DPO
Active preference collection and sample-efficient labeling strategies
Combining DPO with constitutional or rule-based filtering methods
Applying DPO to other generative modalities (vision, audio)
Theoretical research directions: tighter guarantees and generalization bounds

outline.description: A practical chapter guiding the reader through reproducing key experiments. Provide step-by-step instructions, pseudocode, recommended libraries and checkpoints, tips for hyperparameter selection, and troubleshooting common training issues.
sections: Environment setup and required tooling (frameworks, GPUs, checkpoints)
Preparing datasets and preference pairs for each task
Constructing or obtaining a reference policy (SFT or Preferred-FT)
Implementing the DPO loss efficiently (pseudocode and code snippets)
Training loop: optimization, logging, and checkpointing
Evaluation pipelines: generating samples, computing KL and rewards, using GPT-4
Reproducing the sentiment frontier and TL;DR summarization experiments
Troubleshooting guide: common errors and their solutions

outline.description: Provide exercises and project suggestions that reinforce understanding and encourage further exploration. Problems range from derivations to empirical mini-projects suitable for course assignments.
sections: Mathematical exercises: derivations from the textbook (e.g., re-derive key equations)
Proof-based problems: working through the equivalence lemmas and theorem
Implementation tasks: build a toy DPO trainer for a small LM
Empirical projects: compare DPO against PPO on a custom dataset
Exploratory analyses: study beta sensitivity and generalization
Critical thinking prompts: design mitigations for failure modes
Advanced project ideas: multi-turn DPO, synthetic preference generation, cross-modal DPO

outline.description: Supplementary material containing detailed proofs, extended derivations, implementation details, hyperparameter tables, prompts used for GPT-4 and human studies, and additional experimental plots. Useful for readers who want to dive deeper or reproduce results exactly.
sections: Complete mathematical derivations and full proofs of lemmas/theorems
Derivation of the optimal policy (detailed control-as-inference calculus)
Extension to Plackett-Luce and other ranking models
Complete implementation details and hyperparameter settings used in experiments
GPT-4 prompts and human evaluation interface specifications
Additional experimental figures and ablation plots
Reproducibility checklist and links to datasets and code (where available)
